# Goldfish Report — Zoom-Out (Skeptical Architect) — Mode: BRAINSTORM

**Concept under review:** `docs/Plan/EGM-BRAINSTORM-2026-11-11-node-launch/feature_concept.md` — "Node" First Launch — Ride Hidden, User/Operator Split
**Stance:** Strictly read-only. Findings grounded in direct file reads of the repo (2026-11-11).

---

## Overall Verdict

The concept is directionally sound and unusually honest about current state, but its draft-stage risk is **scope creep at the seams, not the core**: components 1 and 4 are near-zero new code (reuse confirmed), component 3 proposes two new screens where one dropdown suffices, and the single open item that could balloon — the hide mechanism — is already 90% decided by a locked ruling that the concept still presents as an open fork. The minimal path touches roughly six code sites plus identity/theme constants.

---

## Findings

**F1 — Severity: Major (Blocker-adjacent)**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI & Code Minimization
**Challenge/Risk:** The "Hide-mechanism choice" open item (concept line 57) presents `platform_config` runtime flag vs build-time `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` flag as a live fork, but the locked ruling (line 37: re-enable "without a store update") already eliminates the build-time branch: with `expo-updates` disabled (`app.config.js` line 33, `enabled: false`) and env inlined at bundle time (AGENTS.md §Testing), an `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` flip requires a new bundle → a store release. Listing it as an open option invites building the wrong thing or re-litigating the ruling at draft.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Collapse the open item to a transport decision only. The flag's *storage* already exists — `platform_config` with fresh-read helpers in `lib/platformConfig.ts` and admin writes via `PATCH /api/admin/config` (AGENTS.md §platform_config). The *client read path* does not exist yet (the only config API routes are `app/api/admin/config+api.ts` and `app/api/admin/tax/config+api.ts`; nothing public). Minimal transport: (a) piggyback one boolean on the existing splash `POST /api/auth/verify-token` call (`app/index.tsx:101–113`) for authenticated cold starts, plus one tiny `[public]` config GET for the unauthenticated welcome surface — or (b) re-enable `expo-updates` in the launch build and make re-enable an OTA bundle. Pick one; do not build a feature-flag framework for a single boolean.

**F2 — Severity: Major**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI & Code Minimization (reuse)
**Challenge/Risk:** Component 3 (concept line 29) reads as two new "first screens" (user login screen + user-first registration screen with operator dropdown). Both surfaces substantially exist: `app/(auth)/welcome.tsx` is already the post-splash first screen with Sign In / Register buttons (lines 65–75), and `app/(auth)/register.tsx` is the user registration form (lines 22–36). "Login as Operator" is also cosmetically heavier than it sounds: every login already flows through the same `phone-entry` OTP, and the gate routes by role afterward (`app/index.tsx:147–156`; `login-as.tsx` `ROLE_HOME`, lines 34–44). The operator/user distinction at login is navigation labeling, not a new auth surface or backend.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Re-skin `welcome.tsx` and `register.tsx` (add the bottom buttons) rather than authoring new screens; the "Register as Operator" dropdown maps onto the existing per-role wizards (concept line 45 itself concedes "no new wizard is required"). Critically: the role→wizard registry **already exists** — `RESUBMIT_WIZARD` in `login-as.tsx:49–53`. The dropdown must consume that single map (promote it to a shared lib if needed) instead of defining a second registry — two sources of truth for role→surface mapping is the architectural dead-end to refuse now.

**F3 — Severity: Major**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI (over-scoped fact in Current-State)
**Challenge/Risk:** Concept line 42 states hiding ride "needs a tab-bar pass." The customer tab bar is not rendered at all: `app/(main)/(customer)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` lines 79–81 set `tabBarStyle: { display: "none" }`. There is no visible tab bar to redesign. Related factual sharpening: the splash's default rider branch **already lands on services-hub** (`app/index.tsx:156` — `redirect("/(main)/(customer)/services-hub")`), so "customer landing is ride" holds only via the login-as rider path and the `(customer)/index.tsx` redirect.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Shrink the open item "tab-bar pass" to its true size: two one-line redirect re-points — `ROLE_HOME.rider` in `login-as.tsx:35` (`/(main)/(customer)/home` → services-hub when hidden) and `app/(main)/(customer)/index.tsx:4` (`Redirect` → `(tabs)/home`) — plus verification that `rides`/`chat` tab screens are otherwise unreachable. This materially shrinks the draft's effort estimate.

**F4 — Severity: Major**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI & Code Minimization
**Challenge/Risk:** The flag's blast radius is genuinely small, and the concept's own gates section (line 50) rewards keeping it that way — but nothing in the concept forbids the classic creep: a per-vertical flag registry, a generic "vertical visibility" abstraction, or a brand-config layer. A platform with exactly one hidden vertical and exactly one brand needs neither.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Budget the hide as **one boolean consumed at ~6 verified sites**: (1) services-hub ride block — `services-hub.tsx:130–179` (one conditional around the `VEHICLE_CATEGORIES` map, import at line 12); (2) `login-as.tsx:35`; (3) `(customer)/index.tsx:4`; (4) splash driver branch `app/index.tsx:147`; (5) `ROLE_HOME.driver` `login-as.tsx:36`; (6) the two hardcoded ride copy strings below (F9). Component 4 is already done — `services-hub.tsx` *is* the services vertical page; "hiding the ride-related options" is item (1) only.

**F5 — Severity: Nit**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI (identity rename)
**Challenge/Risk:** Component 2 could invite a runtime brand/theming abstraction. Unnecessary for a single-brand product.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** The swap is constants only, both sources verified: `theme/goRide.ts` line 1 (`export const colors` — single token source; Node palette from `docs/Image/node_brand_colors.txt`) and `app.config.js` identity fields (name/slug/scheme lines 6–19, bundle ids lines 52 and 61, icon/splash lines 12 and 19). All 13 Node assets confirmed present in `docs/Image/` (glob: `node_app_icon_1024.png`, `node_splash_android_1080x2400.png`, `node_splash_ios_1170x2532.png`, adaptive foreground, etc.). One real dependency to keep on the checklist: the scheme change must update the payment deep-link return consumers (`app/payment/success.tsx`, `app/payment/failure.tsx`; flagged in the concept at line 46 and in `app.config.js:14–17`).

**F6 — Severity: Nit**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI (dead code at launch)
**Challenge/Risk:** The ride-driver-onboarding ruling default (concept line 38) mentions "an existing `driver`-role account at login lands on a neutral surface." The ruling itself notes this is moot — no users exist on any track (line 34). A bespoke "neutral surface" for a population of zero is dead code.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Implement as the hidden-branch of the two existing role routings — splash driver branch (`app/index.tsx:147`) and `ROLE_HOME.driver` (`login-as.tsx:36`) pointing at services-hub when the flag is on. Two lines, no new screen. Build the bespoke surface only if ride re-enables with a real driver population.

**F7 — Severity: Nit**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI (open item that likely dissolves)
**Challenge/Risk:** Open item "SOS/GlobalActionButtons ride-context handling when no ride is active" (concept line 59) budgets verification effort, but the primary surface appears ride-independent: `components/GlobalActionButtons.tsx` SOS is global and role-aware (`useUserRole()` line 147; contacts via `GET /api/sos/contacts` lines 305–330; 999 pre-default line 114; `tel:` dialing line 400) with no visible active-ride dependency in the floating stack.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Reclassify as pure verification (trace ride-screen-local SOS variants), not a work item. If nothing surfaces, delete the open item at draft.

**F8 — Severity: Nit**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI (defer, don't build)
**Challenge/Risk:** Open item "whether any ride-admin screens need launch-time gating" (concept line 58) is a question with a cheap default answer: no. Admin is staff-only; the Copy Truth Rule (AGENTS.md) governs user-facing surfaces, not internal staff tools.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Decide "no gating at launch" at draft and spend zero code. Revisit only if a concrete staff workflow can accidentally trigger ride-side actions.

**F9 — Severity: Nit**
**Dimension:** Contrarian / YAGNI (gates interaction)
**Challenge/Risk:** The concept's "hide, never delete" reasoning (line 50) is correct and matches the repo's gate inventory. Two under-flagged interactions remain: (a) hardcoded ride copy is visible on the first screens regardless of the flag — `welcome.tsx:45` ("Your ride, your way. Get started in seconds.", hard-coded English) and `app/index.tsx:200` ("Your ride, your way") — these violate the spirit of the Node rename and the Copy Truth Rule even before any gating logic exists, and they are exactly the LOCALE-ONLY baseline class in flow-xcheck, so localizing them touches `flow-locale-baseline.json` (a ratchet that must only shrink); (b) Maestro flows asserting ride surfaces stay statically green while runtime-hidden — a green gate does not verify the hidden state.
**Alternative / Reuse Opportunity:** Fold the two strings into the copy sweep (concept open item line 56) with the baseline edit done in the same change; at draft, add one line to the test plan: device verification runs BOTH flag states, ride-flow steps suppressed/annotated via `maestro/tools/flow-xcheck-suppressions.json` where the hidden state makes them unrunnable.

---

## Minimal-Path Summary (what the draft should lock)

1. One flag, one transport (F1), stored in existing `platform_config`, read via verify-token piggyback + one tiny public GET — no framework.
2. ~6 consumer sites (F4/F3/F6) + 2 copy strings (F9) + theme/identity constants (F5) + payment deep-link scheme consumers (F5).
3. Component 3 = re-skin two existing screens + one dropdown reusing the `RESUBMIT_WIZARD` registry (F2).
4. Shrink the open-items list: tab-bar pass → two redirects; SOS → verification only; admin gating → decided "no"; hide mechanism → decided by the ruling.

No concept component requires new backend infrastructure, new DB schema (`user_roles`/`userRoleEnum` at `src/db/schema.ts:58` and `:376–390` already cover the multi-role model the rulings retain), or new wizards. The feature is, at minimum, a re-pointing and re-skinning exercise — keep it there.
